title: Tenant-aware JSON Normalizer and Log Aggregator with Sticky Correlation-ID Rewrite
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: We receive heterogeneous structured logs from SDKs, sidecars, and third-party partners. Field names and timestamp formats vary per client, and transient request IDs make cross-service correlation unreliable. Spikes in per-tenant ingestion cause downstream Loki receivers to drop or reorder entries and make debugging SLA breaches difficult. Goal: Build a tenant-aware ingestion component that normalizes JSON fields on-the-fly, rewrites ephemeral correlation IDs to stable 'sticky' anchors for the duration of a session, and applies quota-aware aggregation/backpressure so downstream storage (Loki/ELK) remains healthy during bursts.
proposal: Introduce a Log Preprocessor microservice in the ingest path that performs: 1) JSON schema normalization via a lightweight configurable mapper (converts timestamp formats to RFC3339, canonicalizes field names: user_id/customer_id -> tenant.user_id), 2) Sticky Correlation-ID mapping (maps ephemeral request IDs to a stable trace_anchor ID with TTL and probabilistic re-association rules), 3) Quota-aware aggregation (per-tenant sampler + merge-mode aggregator that emits 'drop' markers when sampling), 4) Label enrichment for Loki (tenant, env, service, role), and 5) Backpressure signal to sidecars via token-bucket GRPC response with suggested retry/backoff headers.
design_decisions: Keep normalization rules declarative (YAML JSONMap stored in ConfigStore) so product can add mappings without code deploys
Use an in-memory LRU+TTL sticky-id map (hot path) with fallback to Redis for longer-lived sessions to avoid loss on preprocessor restart
Emit deterministic synthetic keys (sha256(ephemeral_id + tenant_id) shortened) as trace_anchor to preserve privacy and ensure idempotency
Apply sampling at the earliest possible stage with configurable policies: deterministic reservoir sampler for errors, rate-based sampler for debug-level logs
Push canonicalized logs to a sharded Kafka topic (keyed by tenant) before downstream consumers (Loki writers), to decouple spikes and enable durable fanout
tradeoffs: In-memory sticky map reduces latency but can lose mappings on pod restart; Redis increases stability but adds latency—chose hybrid approach to balance both
Sampling reduces storage and cost but can obscure rare failure modes; mitigated by error-prioritized reservoir sampling and 'always keep' policy for severity >= ERROR
Normalization is best-effort; some edge-case vendor formats will require later mapping updates (product involvement required)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy preprocessor in us-west-2 for 5% of tenant traffic, forward copy to staging Kafka topic for validation
Phase 2 (validation): Run synthetic traffic harness to verify stable correlation continuity across 3 hops and measure P50/P99 processing latency
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): Increase to 30% then 100% with monitoring gates (error-rate, successful normalization rate, dropped-log fraction), revert on gate failure
Phase 4 (optimize): Tune sampler thresholds and TTLs, add schema mappings observed during canary
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end tests demonstrate correlation continuity: a synthetic trace with ephemeral IDs across three services resolves to single trace_anchor in aggregated logs
Normalization coverage >= 95% for top-10 vendor formats observed in production traffic during canary
Processing latency (preprocessor p50) < 75ms and p99 < 500ms under nominal load
Per-tenant drop marker rate during controlled spikes is below agreed budget (<= 2% of critical-level logs, <= 10% of debug-level logs), with backpressure signaled to sidecars
No increase in Loki write errors attributable to ingest path after rollout (compare pre-rollout baseline)
test_plan: Unit tests for normalization rules and sticky-id generation (deterministic outputs)
Integration test: preprocessor -> kafka -> loki-writer on staging cluster with replayed production payloads
Chaos test: restart preprocessor pods to validate hybrid sticky map fallback to Redis
Load test: hammer ingress at 3x nominal peak to validate quota-aware sampling and downstream stability
Observability checks: dashboards with processing_latency_p50/p99, normalized_count, dropped_count, sticky_hit_rate, redis_p99
metrics_and_dashboards: Dashboards: Grafana 'Ingest v2 - Overview', 'Tenant Bias & Drops', 'Sticky-ID Continuity'
implementation_steps: Create normalization rule DSL and ConfigStore schema (PR #4321)
Implement preprocessor service binary (go) with plugin points for mappers and sampler (PR #4330)
Integrate hybrid sticky-id store: in-memory + Redis (PR #4334)
Add gRPC backpressure contract to sidecar SDKs and update sidecar release notes (SDK PR #1202)
Add kafka sharding and new topic creation with retention policy tweak
Add Grafana panels and Alert rules for normalization-failure-rate and dropped-rate
